name: Flag eligibility, approve the admission, and issue the student and guardian credentials
priorityReason: The decision that turns an applicant into a student. Every downstream module depends on the record it creates.

goal.capability: to judge an applicant on their form and score together, decide the admission, and have the credentials issued
goal.outcome: an admitted child exists as a student and the family can sign in, without anyone re-typing what we already hold

Completes the enrolment once the admission is confirmed.

establishedBy.name: Class, section and academic session structure

preconditions.condition: A numbering pattern is configured, so a student ID and roll number can be generated (BR-6).

postConditions: The applicant carries a recorded eligibility flag with its reason, and a recorded admission decision with its decider and date.
On approval a student record exists, carrying a generated student ID and roll number, and the applicant's form details are on it rather than re-typed.
A guardian account exists with a system-generated guardian ID linked to the family code, so the family can sign in.
The student ID and the guardian credentials have been sent to the contact number and email held on the form, and the send is logged.

On rejection the inquiry is closed with the reason recorded, the family is informed, and no student record or account exists.
The applicant's temporary ID is retired. Everything from here uses the student ID.

businessRules.rule: The admission form and the test score are shown together. Neither is sufficient on its own, and a decision taken on one without the other is the failure this rule prevents.
Eligibility and approval are separate acts by separate people. The School Admin flags who is worth putting forward; the Principal decides who is admitted.
An eligibility flag requires a reason, whether eligible or not. A flag with no reason tells the Principal nothing and cannot be defended later.
Rejection requires a reason. The family is told why, so an unexplained rejection is not permitted.
Approval creates the student record from the applicant's form. Nothing the family already supplied is re-typed.
On approval the system generates the student ID and roll number according to the configured pattern. They are never typed or chosen by a user, and are never reused.

A guardian account is created with a system-generated guardian ID linked to the family code. Where the family code already exists, because a sibling is enrolled, the existing guardian is reused rather than a second one created.
A section at capacity refuses admission into it. The Principal may choose another section, or approve and place the student later.
Credentials are issued with a temporary password that must be changed at first sign-in. The student ID and the guardian credentials are sent to the contact number and email held on the form.
A bulk approval covers only applicants already flagged eligible, and each is approved individually inside the batch. One failure does not abandon the rest, and each outcome is reported separately.
A decision is never edited. A correction is a further recorded decision, so the sequence of what was decided and when survives.
An applicant recorded absent from the test may still be decided on, but the absence is shown to the decider rather than treated as a score.

transitions.condition: Approved, a section with capacity is assigned, and the records are created (BR-5, BR-8).
The flag is revised with a new reason. Both flags stay in the history.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicants awaiting eligibility
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the admission form and the test score together, with the attendance where the applicant was absent.

basicFlow.userAction: Flags the applicant eligible or not eligible and records the reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the flag, its reason and who set it, and puts eligible applicants to the Principal.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens an eligible applicant, or selects a batch of them on the bulk approval screen.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the form, the score and the eligibility flag with its reason.

basicFlow.navigation: Applicant decision → Assign section → Approve admission
basicFlow.userAction: Assigns a section and approves the admission.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the section has capacity, then records the decision, the decider and the date.
Creates the student record from the applicant's form, generates the student ID and roll number, creates or reuses the guardian and family, and enrols the student.
Creates the student and guardian accounts with system-generated usernames and a temporary password.
Sends the student ID and the guardian credentials to the contact number and email held on the form, and logs the send.
Closes the inquiry as admitted, links it to the student record, and retires the temporary ID.

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal approves a whole batch at once
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Bulk admission approval
alternateFlows.behaviour: Only applicants already flagged eligible may be selected. Each is approved individually inside the batch, with its own record creation and credential issue. One failure is reported and does not abandon the rest (BR-10).
The reason is recorded, the inquiry is closed and the family is informed. No student record, guardian account or credential is created (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: A sibling is already enrolled and the family code exists
alternateFlows.behaviour: The existing guardian and family code are reused rather than a second household created, so siblings bill and are messaged together (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The chosen section is at capacity
alternateFlows.behaviour: Another section is chosen, or the admission is approved without a section and the student is placed later. Nothing is over-filled (BR-8).
The existing student record is reactivated and linked to the new class and session instead of a new one being created. The previous history stays attached (UC-02-09).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin revises an eligibility flag
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new flag is recorded with its own reason. Both flags stay in the history, so a changed judgement is visible rather than hidden.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
